subject: Separate Detection Functions v.s. one detection function

messages.author: cfb364282622bc71
messages.subject: Separate Detection Functions v.s. one detection function
parts:
Dear All,

I have three years of line transect data, which I want to use to produce density surface models for each year. I initially wanted to produce a separate detection function for each year. The methodologies and vessels used across years did not differ, however observers differed every year, and so thought detection rate may also differ. However, I have noticed there is evidence of spiked data when looking at count with distance for each year, and furthermore, one of the years has only ~50 observations. If I remember correctly, Buckland et al.,2001 recommend at least 60-80 observations, especially if there is evidence of spiked data. Is it ok to compute a single detection function, and then apply them separately during the DSM stage? Or is it still best to have separate detection functions for each year?

 

Thanks for your help

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Separate Detection Functions v.s. one detection function
parts:
Raph

One possibility:  before moving to the dsm analysis, perform conventional distance sampling of the two years of data, treating each year as a stratum.  Fit two models: one with stratum-specific detection functions, the other with a pooled detection function.  Use AIC to assess whether the pooled or stratum-specific model is preferable.  With that decision made, then move on to the second stage dsm modelling.
